answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a ledge as the anchor of the cost.
